identity.differences: Same brand and expression (Jameson Irish Whiskey, the standard blend; no age statement, no vintage, no pack suffix). No supplier evidence on either member: 0 invoice lines, 0 price-list rows, no supplier on any alias, and the only purchase order (CANCELLED, Alma Avalon 27 Aug 2026, 'No known supplier') lists both. The one real difference checked is bottle size, and it is conflicting metadata rather than evidence of two bottlings: the May record is named '1000ML BOTTLE' with measurePerCountUnit 1000 and avgCost 7754 (its notes store cost per ml 0.07754); the floor record has measurePerCountUnit 750 while its own notes say 'Cost taken from the Loaded count (drinks.json): 1 700 mL = $54.28' and its Loaded import lines (St Alma 2026-03-31/06-02/06-30, Alma Avalon 06-02/06-30) carry the unit '700 mL'. The two costs are exactly proportional (5428 = 0.7 x 7754, per-ml 0.07754 on both), so one was derived from the other; the 2025 Historical Bar Stocktake sheets valued the bottle at 8529-8530c = 7754 x 1.1 (the 1 L price inc GST) and the floor record's own latestCostCents is 7760 (31 May 2026), so the independently sourced price is the 1 L one and Loaded's $54.28 is a pro-rata, which points to the venue buying 1 L bottles (the audit's naming guide already uses 'Jameson Irish Whiskey 1L' as its example). What settles identity regardless of size: every sheet from Aug 2025 to Oct 2026 carries exactly ONE Jameson line per venue and the quantity is continuous (St Alma 1/1/1/1/1 on the 2025 sheets, 0.5 on 31 Mar 2026, 1 on 2 Jun, 30 Jun, 1 Aug, 31 Aug and 1 Oct 2026; Alma Avalon 0.5/0.5/0.4/0.5/0.45 in 2025, 0.5 on 2 Jun and 30 Jun, 0.38 on 1 Sep, 0.47 on 1 Oct 2026); a 700 mL and a 1 L Jameson never appear side by side, and the May record's notes list the floor name as an alias ('Also known as: jameson • Jameson • jameson irish whiskey • Jameson Irish Whiskey'). One product counted under two records; the bottle size is a field to correct on the survivor, not a second product.
